title: Earlier Chicago generation: Quartell, Don Murray and Glenn Scoville
summary: They discuss Quartell's brothers, tenor players Murray and Scoville, and how Murray began.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: There was a generation of Chicagoans before the Austens, and you mentioned Quartell. Are you familiar with his brothers?
He plays trombone, and the younger brother plays clarinet.
I knew he had brothers, but I didn't.

Tinny Scoville, Glenn Scoville, was another tenor player who was a contemporary of Don Murray's. Don Murray used to play a scene melody in a Presbyterian church in Evanston. That's how he got started. And then he changed to clarinet when he joined Go Cat. But he and Scoville both played with the Rhythm Kings.
